response: Causal chain for the checklist-plus-boundary-checks composition: (1) instruction present -> (2) pre-code extraction yields the numbered requirement list -> (3) implementation with the list as external memory -> (4) per-item executed probes, choosing boundary or degenerate inputs where the item implies them -> (5) probe failures self-correct in place -> (6) pass rate rises through two additive channels: omissions caught at extraction, mishandled boundaries caught at probing. The composition's specific mechanism — spec-keyed probe selection — matters because it replaces the sibling arm's fixed category list with the task's own structure: coverage scales with requirement density instead of category applicability. Fragile links: turn arithmetic (10-15 probes plus implementation versus a 15-turn cap forces batching, and batched probes drift shallow), and probe-selection quality (items rarely state their boundary cases explicitly; inferring them re-introduces the reader who missed them the first time). Supporting evidence needed: positive paired delta; transcripts showing per-item probes with non-trivial inputs; failure audit showing recovered trials correspond to probe-caught boundary faults. Disconfirming: candidate arms hitting the turn cap at elevated rates (overhead dominates), or probes present but uniformly trivial with unchanged pass rate (shallow compliance). Attribution caveat stands: without parent and sibling arms in the same study, a positive result cannot be decomposed into its two channels.
